thesis: GBTG's volume spike (10.9x average) and proximity to its 52-week high reflect trading dynamics around its pending $9.50/share take-private deal (stockholder-approved, expected to close late 2026) rather than a fresh operating catalyst; the current price sits within two cents of the deal price, leaving negligible spread to capture. invalidation: Deal is renegotiated at a materially different price, litigation succeeds in delaying or blocking the close, or the merger closes without incident and removes any residual thesis

thesis: GitLab's Q2 FY27 beat-and-raise (revenue $286.3M, EPS $0.24, guidance raised on AI-driven demand and the new Flex/hybrid-consumption pricing model) drove a 17%+ post-earnings pop and a string of analyst target increases (UBS to $40, Truist to $40, BofA to $45); this suggests durable enterprise AI traction. thesis: Dell's volume spike (6.2x average) accompanies a confirmed Q2 FY27 blowout — record $47B revenue (+58% YoY), EPS $6.34 (+273% YoY), and FY27 guidance raised well above consensus on a record $95B AI-server backlog — a specific, already-disclosed catalyst. However, Dell's FY2025 10-K disclosed a restatement of prior-period cost-of-goods-sold (understated by roughly $200M in FY2024 and $148M in FY2025 through Q3) tied to unrecorded supplier credits, with an identified material weakness in internal controls as of Jan 31, 2025 — a governance event from within the last 3 years that keeps conviction capped regardless of how strong today's print is.
invalidation: AI-server backlog growth stalls, guidance is walked back, or the disclosed material weakness is found to have recurred in a subsequent filing

invalidation: The post-earnings selloff stabilizes and reverses on confirmed fundamentals, or subsequent guidance shows the growth deceleration analysts are pricing in

thesis: Vertiv's pullback traces to a confirmed July 29 Q2 print — revenue missed on supply-chain timing even as adjusted EPS beat and full-year guidance was raised across every key metric (revenue to $14B, adjusted EPS to $6.70) — compounded by a broader AI-infrastructure sector selloff through August. thesis: AMD's 60-day decline is driven mainly by sector-wide semiconductor sentiment (AI-overspending fears) and company-specific competitive concerns — a major customer reportedly sourcing AI chips from a rival, and reports that China's DeepSeek is developing its own AI processor — even though AMD's own recent quarterly results beat estimates; investors sold anyway on already-elevated expectations (a ~123x trailing P/E versus a ~35x sector average). invalidation: AMD confirms material AI-accelerator customer losses in its own disclosures, or the stock stabilizes and the sector-wide selloff reverses on confirmed easing AI-capex concerns

thesis: SpaceX's 60-day price move is net negative despite a mid-window rebound — an Aug 8 lockup-expiration non-event plus a confirmed $16.8B joint Tesla/SpaceX Texas semiconductor-fab (Terafab) investment drove a 15.8% one-day pop, but shares still trade only modestly above the June IPO price and remain well off the post-IPO high. As a company that IPO'd less than three months ago, the fundamental base for a confident directional read is thin, and its governing documents route securities claims to mandatory arbitration rather than court — an unusual structural factor worth noting even though it isn't a scheduled litigation event.
invalidation: Shares establish a sustained trend meaningfully above or below the IPO price on confirmed fundamentals from a subsequent earnings print, giving more than one quarter of public-company history to judge

thesis: NVIDIA's 60-day gain follows a confirmed Aug 26 Q2 earnings beat with FY2028 revenue growth guided to ~70%, well above the ~44% analysts expected, driving a broad chip-sector rally. The clearest counter-evidence is a certified securities class action (class certified March 25, 2026) alleging historical misclassification of crypto-mining-related GPU revenue in 2021-2022 disclosures; that matter concerns legacy accounting characterization from several years ago with no scheduled near-term ruling or hearing, and doesn't bear on the current AI-datacenter demand the new guidance is built on.
invalidation: FY2028 guidance is walked back in a subsequent print, or the securities class action produces an adverse near-term ruling that raises new disclosure concerns about current-period revenue
